BAY PROCEDURE Tacoma RV Center · Document Library CONCERN icing up on rear wall - only about half from the top down MODEL Furrion FCR10 DATE 2026-10-09 WO# - PRIMARY Furrion fridge service manual, Ice and Moisture section (Fig. 36). VISUAL FLOWCHART Ice or frost is on the rear wall of the fridge. Light sheet only on the back wall? Normal cycling. You are done. Is the dial at max? Set the dial to about 4 to 5. Dry. Run overnight. Full defrost. Dry. Clear the rear drain and trough. Does the gasket fail a dollar-bill test? Repair or reseat the gasket. Recheck 24 to 48 hours. Heavy frost return after about 1 month? Replace the cooling unit after that month. Moisture path confirmed. You are done. YES NO YES NO YES NO YES NO BAY PROCEDURE Bay order · Tacoma RV Center UNIT ID Brand: Furrion Model: FCR10 Serial: ____________________ WHAT THIS PATTERN USUALLY MEANS A frost or ice band on the upper rear wall, with the lower rear often clearer, is a common Furrion fridge complaint. It is usually moisture on a cold evaporator surface from the door seal, humidity, setpoint, airflow, or the drain. A light sheet of ice or moisture only on the back wall is normal cycling: the cabinet condenses, freezes, and thaws. This pattern by itself is not proof of a sealed-system failure. BAY ORDER (DO THIS FIRST) Step 1: Open the fridge and note the ice or moisture pattern Do this: 1. Photograph it. 2. A light sheet only on the back wall is normal cycling. 3. Stop here. 4. Heavy, halfway-down, or other-surface frost means keep going. Step 2: Record the dial setting and the fridge and freezer cavity temperatures Do this: 1. If the dial is at max, set it to about 4 to 5. 2. Towel-dry the melt and let the fridge run overnight. 3. Then look at the pattern again. 4. If ice starts to melt at mid setpoint, stay on the moisture path. 5. If the dial is already mid, go to the defrost next. Step 3: Do a full manual defrost Do this: 1. Power the unit off, open both doors, and use towels. 2. Do not scrape, do not use a heat gun. 3. Do not set hot-water pans in the cabinet. 4. When the ice is gone, go to the dry-and-drain step. Step 4: Dry the cabinet completely Do this: 1. Clear the rear drain and trough with a soft plastic probe only so melt water can leave. 2. If water backs up, keep clearing until it leaves. 3. Then go to the gasket. 4. If the drain is already open, go to the gasket next. Step 5: Check the door gasket with a dollar-bill test around the full perimeter Do this: 1. Check the hinges, latch, and door alignment. 2. If the bill slides out with no drag, reseat or replace the gasket. 3. Set the dial to about 4 to 5. 4. Leave a rear-wall air gap. 5. Recheck in 24 to 48 hours. 6. If the gasket holds, set the dial mid. 7. Leave the air gap, and recheck in 24 to 48 hours. Step 6: Check the cabinet after 24 to 48 hours Do this: 1. If frost is gone or just a back-wall sheet, you are done. 2. The fix was mid setpoint, a holding gasket, and a clear drain. 3. Did heavy frost return with a mid dial, good gasket, and clear drain? 4. Leave the cooling unit in place. 5. Dry the cabinet again and watch door-open time and humidity for about a month. BAY PROCEDURE Bay order continued BAY ORDER (CONTINUED) Step 7: If ice or moisture persists after drying and waiting 1 month, replace the unit Do this: 1. Replace the cooling unit only after that month. 2. That is the confirmed correction. 3. If the heavy frost is gone after that watch, you are done. CITED MANUAL FIGURES Fig. 36 rear-wall frost pattern, views A and B -- Furrion FCR08/FCR10 SM CCD-0008122 p.36 DO NOT - Do not knife the ice off the rear wall. - Do not assume a sealed-system failure from top-half frost alone. - Do not leave the cabinet wet after defrost.
